topics.topic: Credential newline stripping, forbidden characters, Unicode acceptance, and wire encoding
questions: Which Unicode or byte ranges count as control characters, and how are LF, CRLF, multiple trailing line endings, NUL and C1 controls handled?
Exactly which trailing sequence is removed, what happens with multiple trailing newlines, and which Unicode characters count as control characters?
May a credential contain non-ASCII Unicode, and if so, what exact bytes are sent in the HTTP header; otherwise, which character set must validation accept?
Exactly which trailing newline is removed, which Unicode or byte values are forbidden, and how is an accepted non-ASCII credential encoded on the wire?

judgement.why: The exact newline sequence, character repertoire, and HTTP wire encoding are encoding and field-constraint decisions for State 6.

topics.topic: Credential-file and decoded-value size limits and resulting failure
questions: What maximum is applied to a secret file and its decoded credential value, and what exact failure occurs when it is exceeded?
What is the maximum credential-file/value size, and does exceeding it produce `credential_unresolved`, prevent kernel startup, or cause an internal error?
At what size is a credential file refused as `credential_unresolved`, and is it read with a hard bound before allocation?

quotes:
A credential is resolved only when a request to its service is built: its
secret file is read then, without following a symbolic link, and must be a
regular file owned by the kernel's user with no permission for group or
others; its content decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline, is the
value.

Every global ceiling is one release constant `RELEASE_CEILING_<NAME>`, the
name below in upper case, delivered to code as a data-provider constant
(SPEC_STANDARD 15.3.1, 6.10: one exact entry is one scalar constant; owner,
2026-10-03, raised by the pre-contract data closure).
judgement.divergence: One implementation reads credential files without a dedicated bound and may send an arbitrarily large header or exhaust resources; another imposes a bound and returns `credential_unresolved`, which the owner and target service notice.
judgement.why: The text requires reading the file but neither assigns it a release ceiling nor determines the observable outcome of an oversized credential.

topics.topic: Exact inventory and mapping of fixed MCP surface operations
questions: Are the omitted actions separate operations on the fixed surface, aliases or modes of the listed operations, or intentionally unavailable?
Are all State 0 primary actions distinct callable surface operations, or are the actions omitted from K-11 unavailable or folded into its named operations?
What exact typed MCP operations exist, and are the additional State 0 actions separate operations or variants hidden under the shorter K-11 verbs?

quotes:
The one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp` (K-11), one per State 0
action.

| `capture_failed_execution` | owner, author | `runs.capture_failed_execution` |
| `roll_back_slot` | owner, author | `functions.roll_back_slot` |
| `propose_binding` | agent | `bindings.propose_binding` |
| `accept_binding` | owner | `bindings.accept_binding` |
| `compose_flow_version` | agent | `flows.compose_flow_version` |
| `prove_flow_version` | agent | `flows.prove_flow_version` |
| `activate_flow_version` | owner, agent (`read` only, A06) | `flows.activate_flow_version` |
| `start_run` | owner, agent | `runs.start_run` |
| `resume_run` | owner, agent | `runs.resume_run` |
| `release_run` | owner, agent | `runs.release_run` |
| `decide_effect_approval` | owner | `runs.continue_after_approval` |
judgement.why: The later public API catalogue makes each State 0 action a separate MCP operation and explicitly lists the actions omitted from K-11's shorthand.

topics.topic: Ordering of derived skip and upstream-failure records relative to ready-node execution
questions: After an execution changes several downstream nodes, are all newly skipped or upstream-failed nodes recorded before another ready node executes, after all ready nodes, or interleaved in one declared global order?

When propagation makes some nodes skipped or `upstream_failed` while other nodes are ready to execute, are all synthetic records written immediately before selecting another executable node, or are they interleaved in the global node-id schedule?
At each advancement step, are all newly derivable skip and upstream-failure records written before selecting a ready node, after ready nodes are exhausted, or interleaved in one common node-id order?

judgement.why: This is the same ordering question already decided by P16, and its deciding later-state passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Ordering of non-executable propagation and ready-node execution
quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] After each function element MUST write one RecordRunProgressChange holding that element's execution, its StoredValues and SpooledFiles, and every skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed record that became determined, executions sorted by (node_id, map_index), with status running; after an operation element, whose concluding record effects wrote, the next RecordRunProgressChange holds the records it made non-executable.
precedent.why: The later run contract requires newly determined skipped and upstream-failed records to be written immediately after the element that determined them, before the advancement loop selects another executable node.

topics.topic: Unit and truncation basis for disclosed failure-detail length
questions: Is the disclosed failure_detail length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
What does the disclosed length measure: Unicode characters, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, or UTF-8 bytes after truncation to `failure_detail_bytes_max`?
Is the disclosed length measured in Unicode scalar values, UTF-8 bytes, or the stored truncated detail's characters or bytes?

judgement.why: This is the same disclosed failure-detail length question already decided by P6.

precedent.topic: Unit and processing stage used for disclosed failure-detail length
quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
precedent.why: The later note specifies the UTF-8 byte length of the retained failure_detail.

topics.topic: Atomicity and ordering of mapped-output materialization when an aggregate exceeds the value limit
questions: In what order are mapped outputs and their fan-out edges materialized, and if one delivered list exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`, may any other output already have been delivered or must all deliverable lists be checked before any delivery?

If one mapped output list fits and another exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`, are any fitting outputs delivered or exposed as produced, or does the aggregate failure discard every output of that mapped node atomically?

quotes:
A value list is one
StoredValue, the JSON array of the elements' values in element order, whose
`value_schema` is the array schema with the port's schema as `items`, as
for every value of a `many` port (M21),
written by `runs` when the list is first delivered — never in an element's
own store change, which for an operation element is `effects'` — and
named, like any value, by the records that receive it; a list whose
canonical bytes exceed `stored_value_bytes_max` is not written: the node is
then failed for its dependants, which conclude `upstream_failed` and write
that record (A15 rule 1), derived like the list from the elements'
records, which stay as they are (A15 rule 4).

Only a list that is
delivered — to a node or a flow output — is measured; an output no edge
takes fails nothing.

An element that does not
      succeed keeps no output: its NodeExecution names none, a value it produced
   is not stored, and the files its attempt spooled are discarded: no
   SpooledFile record names them and nothing reads them.
judgement.divergence: One implementation validates every deliverable aggregate before publishing any, so an oversized output exposes none; another publishes fitting outputs in an unspecified delivery order before discovering the oversized output, which downstream operation nodes, callers, and trace readers can notice.
judgement.why: The rules say when each list is first measured and that the mapped node fails, but do not order multiple output deliveries or state an all-before-any aggregate check.

topics.topic: Bytes and framing counted by the surface request-size limit
questions: Does surface_request_bytes_max count the complete encoded MCP/JSON-RPC message, only the operation payload, decoded string bytes, or some other byte sequence, and does it include the token and transport framing?

Which bytes count toward `surface_request_bytes_max`: the complete MCP transport frame, the JSON-RPC/MCP message encoding, or only the encoded typed-operation arguments, and how is the count obtained when the MCP library supplies an already-decoded object?

judgement.why: This is the same MCP request-size boundary question already decided by P14.

precedent.topic: MCP authentication envelope, transport, endpoint, and request-size byte accounting
quotes: serve_kernel: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST call run_start_sequence with config_path, the process's one command-line argument, and open the MCP entrance — MCP over streamable HTTP at the mcp_listen_address of the returned Installation, one tool per catalogue operation — only after it returned; while serving it reads one HTTP request at a time, takes the presented token from its Authorization header in the Bearer form (None when the header is absent or not in that form), passes the body bytes and that token to answer_request and writes back the bytes it returns.

answer_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record; the message names a catalogue operation and fits that operation's request model with no unknown field and every bound below, else invalid_request; the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else not_permitted; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1).
precedent.why: The later surface contract selects streamable HTTP, carries the token in an Authorization Bearer header, and measures the HTTP request body bytes passed as `request_bytes`.

topics.topic: Disclosure-class derivation for operation outputs, empty executions, and failure details
questions: What disclosure class does an operation execution with no inputs and no outputs have, including for classifying its failure_detail?
When an operation receives a higher-class input but declares a lower-class output, does the output take the binding's declared class or retain the highest input class?
For an empty mapped operation node, does each empty output list take the binding output's declared class or the highest class among the node's inputs?

quotes:
At run time a value's class is set by the one rule of M21: a flow input takes
its port's class, a constant its declared class, a function output the highest
class its execution actually received, a binding output the class the binding
declares, a trial case's input its contract input port's class and its
expected output the highest class of the case's inputs. No function, edge or flow construct lowers a class.

A mapped node over an empty list runs nothing, asks nothing and sends
nothing; it writes one NodeExecution `succeeded` — its first record, so number
1 by A11 rule 1 — with no `map_index`, `executed` naming what it pins and every output an empty list. A
`many` file port carries a list of files; inside the sandbox it is a list of
`bytes` (A03). A mapped node concludes only when every element has concluded. It succeeded
when every element succeeded, and its outputs are then lists in element order,
      each list of the highest class among its elements (A07); an empty list
takes the highest class among the node's inputs — the list it mapped over
and every other input — as an execution of the node would have received
them (M21), so no class is lowered;
judgement.why: For an empty mapped operation whose input class differs from its declared output class, one passage assigns the binding output's declared class while the other assigns the highest input class.

topics.topic: Retry and digest behavior after a failed token-list configuration re-read
questions: After a token-list re-read fails, when is another re-read attempted if the configuration bytes do not change?
After changed configuration bytes fail validation, what digest is remembered, and must the same unchanged invalid bytes be parsed again on every request so that a later repair is detected reliably?

judgement.why: This is the same failed token-list reread and retained-digest question already decided by P17.

precedent.topic: State retention and retry behavior after an invalid token-configuration reread
quotes: current_token_list: [BEHAVIOR] On every call MUST read the configuration file's bytes and compare their SHA-256 with the last read digest; when equal it returns the kept list unchanged (none stays none); when different, or when the file cannot be read, it re-reads the file and applies exactly four checks: the file can be read and parses as a JSON object with owner_token and agent_tokens of the Installation types, every token is at least the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant long, no two tokens are equal, and no two agent tokens have the same name; the new digest becomes the last read digest, and when the file cannot be read the last read digest is cleared, so the next readable bytes are always re-read.

current_token_list: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] When all four checks hold, the re-read's tokens replace the kept list; when any fails the kept list becomes none and the old list is discarded, since it may hold a revoked token; a re-read takes only the token list, and no other field of the kept Installation changes until a restart.
precedent.why: The later contract says invalid readable bytes become the last-read digest, so unchanged invalid bytes are not reparsed and the retained token list remains none.

topics.topic: Run finalization when failures coexist with unresolved waits
questions: If one branch has failed and every remaining unfinished branch is waiting for approval, service recovery or outcome resolution, does the run end failed or remain awaiting_approval/pending?
If a run has a failed branch and an independent element still waiting, does it end `failed` immediately or remain `awaiting_approval` or `pending` until the wait is resolved?

quotes:
The run is
`failed` when no node can run any more and some node failed, `succeeded` when every
node and output concluded successfully.

When nothing can execute and nothing waits, the run ends: `succeeded` when every node concluded
succeeded or `skipped_by_guard`; otherwise `failed`.

While some elements wait, every other ready node keeps executing within the
request (K-09); the run then rests `awaiting_approval` when any element waits
for the owner's approval, otherwise `pending`.
judgement.why: M19 makes an existing failure sufficient once no node can currently run, while A13 requires all waits to be gone and otherwise keeps the run resting.

topics.topic: Scheduler eligibility, semantic finality, and retry rules for concluded or waiting nodes and mapped elements
questions: Exactly which existing conclusions and waiting states exclude an unmapped node from the ready set, and when may a service_unreachable or resolved-not_applied element become eligible for another attempt?

Which nodes are scheduler candidates when their inputs are present but they are concluded, partially concluded, or waiting, so the scheduler neither repeatedly selects them nor retries waits outside the permitted request?
Does `concluded record` mean any existing NodeExecution or only a NodeExecution whose combined EffectAttempt state makes the element semantically final?
After an unknown outcome is resolved `not_applied`, is the element waiting, succeeded, or failed for A13 readiness and run completion?

quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST read the Run by identity, its pinned graph with read_flow_version, and its trace with read_records through ExecutionsOfRun, and derive every element's conclusion from the trace: a function element from its NodeExecution's status, an operation element from operation_element_conclusion. If any NodeExecution of the run is refused_by_owner it reaches nothing and ends the run refused. Otherwise it executes one node at a time until no node can execute, then writes the rest or end state in one RecordRunProgressChange.

advance_run: [BEHAVIOR] A function element is executed with execute_function_element; an operation element is reached with reach_operation_element, given a RunContext of the run_id, the pinned flow_version_id and started_under the store_position of the FlowActivation read with ActivationBeforeRun, whose absence is raised as StoreInternalError; operation elements that wait are not reached again here.

operation_element_conclusion: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Decides from the latest NodeExecution of the element, the one with the highest attempt_number, in this order: succeeded concludes succeeded with that record's outputs; outcome_unknown with its EffectAttempt applied concludes succeeded with no outputs when the binding has no output ports and otherwise failed with status outcome_unknown and detail applied_outputs_unknown; any status other than succeeded, service_unreachable and outcome_unknown concludes failed with that status and detail_code; then an approval of the element with status requested makes it wait with reason owner_approval and that approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt resolved not_applied waits with reason owner_approval and no approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown; then service_unreachable waits with reason service_unreachable; with no NodeExecution and no requested approval the element is not reached.

advance_run: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them, constants to their port, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text. A mapped node, once selected, takes its elements in list order, executing every element with no concluded record that does not wait, before the next node is selected; a waiting or failed element does not stop the elements after it, and a concluded element is never executed again.
judgement.why: The later run contract derives semantic conclusions from the trace, excludes waiting operation elements from ordinary advancement, forbids re-executing concluded elements, and classifies resolved `not_applied` as waiting for approval.

topics.topic: Startup validation and loading requirements for selected manifest instances
questions: Must startup read every selected service's manifest instance to check credential-header collisions, and what happens if that manifest or instance is absent or invalid at startup?
Does an invalid selected-instance name stop kernel startup, count as no selected instance, or become `instance_address_missing` only when that service is used?

quotes:
No credential header has, case-insensitively, the name of a required header of
its instance or one of `KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES`, `host` included; reads
installation and manifest only (A09 rule 1). The services checked are those the
installation holds a credential for, in `service_id` code-point order; for
each, the kernel-set names are compared first, without reading the manifest;
then, only when the installation selects an instance for it, its manifest
record is read and that instance's required headers compared. A service with
no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name,
fails nothing here: it is not invocable at send (A09 rule 6).

`refused` naming the first failing service, services taken in `service_id`
code-point order and each one's manifest record read in its turn — an
unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5),
fails at its service; the start stops.
judgement.why: The later startup contract specifies which credential-bearing services require manifest reads, when manifest faults stop startup, and that a missing selected-instance name does not stop startup but makes the service uninvocable.

topics.topic: Symlink-safe traversal and same-descriptor validation of secret and configuration files
questions: Must every path component be opened without following symlinks and the ownership/type/mode checks apply to the same opened file descriptor, or is only the final path entry protected?
Must every path component be opened without following symlinks, and must ownership, mode, and bytes all be checked and read from the same open file descriptor?

quotes:
The file
must be a regular file, not a symbolic link, owned by the kernel's user, with
no permission for group or others; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.

A credential is resolved only when a request to its service is built: its
secret file is read then, without following a symbolic link, and must be a
regular file owned by the kernel's user with no permission for group or
others; its content decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline, is the
value.
judgement.divergence: One implementation protects only the final pathname and performs separate check and read operations; another traverses every component without following links and validates and reads one opened descriptor, which an attacker racing path replacement and the owner relying on secret integrity can notice.
judgement.why: The passages prohibit a symbolic-link target but do not define ancestor traversal or bind validation and reading to the same opened file.

topics.topic: Validation scope required for a live token-list configuration re-read
questions: On a live re-read, does `parsed` require the entire installation configuration to satisfy its schema, or only syntactically valid configuration containing a valid token-list section?
Does a token-list re-read require the entire installation configuration to satisfy its schema, or only enough structure to parse and validate the token list?

quotes: current_token_list: [BEHAVIOR] On every call MUST read the configuration file's bytes and compare their SHA-256 with the last read digest; when equal it returns the kept list unchanged (none stays none); when different, or when the file cannot be read, it re-reads the file and applies exactly four checks: the file can be read and parses as a JSON object with owner_token and agent_tokens of the Installation types, every token is at least the imported ACCESS_TOKEN_LENGTH_MIN constant long, no two tokens are equal, and no two agent tokens have the same name; the new digest becomes the last read digest, and when the file cannot be read the last read digest is cleared, so the next readable bytes are always re-read.

current_token_list: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] When all four checks hold, the re-read's tokens replace the kept list; when any fails the kept list becomes none and the old list is discarded, since it may hold a revoked token; a re-read takes only the token list, and no other field of the kept Installation changes until a restart.
judgement.why: The later installation contract requires a JSON object containing token fields of the Installation types and validates only those token-list facts during a live reread.
